source.snippet: There is a rather-niche set of people, organizations or government agencies, which, for bureaucratic or personal reasons, cannot receive email - and will only receive either regular mail or facsimilie (fax). Suppose I want to arrange it so that sending email to some address results in a fax being sent to a known, fixed, fax number (i.e. phone number, with a fax machine connected on the other side). I know there are quite a few websites for offer the opposite, i.e. an artificial fax number where...

problem_statement: Professionals and businesses that must communicate with government agencies or regulated entities that only accept fax have no simple, self-hostable background service to automatically forward emails to a fixed fax number, forcing manual workarounds.
target_segment: Legal, healthcare, and compliance professionals at SMBs who regularly submit documents to government agencies or regulated counterparties that mandate fax
notes: Buyer signal: professional/business context dealing with regulatory/government fax mandates — this is a recurring operational cost. Existing SaaS fax services (eFax, HelloFax, RingCentral Fax) charge monthly fees, indicating willingness to pay. The specific gap is an email-triggered, background, programmable forwarding service rather than a manual send-each-time UI. Single signal but structurally persistent pain for legal/healthcare/government-adjacent businesses.
